title: New American Ensemble’s production of Ivanov at the West End Theatre ...
transcript: It's kind of astonishing the sheer number of bad decisions collectively made by all of the characters in this Chekhov play. In this production from the New American Ensemble, a man named Nikolai has really lost his zest for life, though he's not the only one. Chekhov is fascinated by suffering and this play has it in droves. Characters suffer from marital strain, illness, financial troubles, or just plain boredom. It’s kind of a melodrama and the suffering is real, but it's also hilarious. I found the first half hour or so to be a slog, but once you're settled into the lives of these characters and all of their idiosyncrasies, it's actually quite entertaining. And although it is a period piece, there's something timeless about how people are reckless and foolish when they're desperate — in this case, desperate to feel something. If you don't enjoy Chekhov in general, I can't promise you'll enjoy this. But otherwise, the fantastic performances and well-calibrated comedy elevate this at times tedious play. While not always riveting, I felt it was worth my time. With that, another program for my collection.
